5888189.reason: Greedy builds each pile as a strictly decreasing chain of strengths, ignoring that a box of strength x can hold x boxes (equal strengths can stack under a larger capacity); on 0010 (four 1s, six 2s) it makes 6 piles instead of 4.

5898411.reason: Tracks pile capacity only via the newest box (ml = a[j]+1, l reset to 1) instead of the minimum remaining capacity of all boxes in the pile, so piles are over-filled and too few piles counted; 0021 prints 1 instead of 3.

9089117.reason: Answers the maximum frequency of a single strength value, ignoring capacity constraints of piles; 0010 (four 1s, six 2s) prints 6 instead of 4.

9126570.reason: Places each box on the first pile whose top strength is strictly smaller, i.e. piles are strictly increasing chains with no capacity counting; this equals max frequency, so 0010 prints 6 instead of 4.

9245036.reason: b[i] starts at i and adds count[i], so max(b[i]-i) is just the maximum frequency of one strength value, not the minimum pile count; 0010 prints 6 instead of 4.
